item.title: Heads-up: newly-granted PBS ACLs are cached up to 5s — scripted PVE storage adds need a retry, not a sleep
item.author: invalid@example.com (Ivan The Geek)
item.dc:creator: Ivan The Geek
item.content:encoded:
CORRECTION, 2026-08-30 - the figure originally in the title and below was wrong. Proxmox staff have confirmed the ACL is cached for up to 5 seconds, not the ~1 s I measured - see Robert Obkircher's reply. A single probe measures where it landed inside the cache window, not the width of the window. item.title: PVE9.x Debian13 LXC /tmp
item.author: invalid@example.com (drevilish)
item.dc:creator: drevilish
item.content:encoded:
I noticed an issue where I was experiencing a lot of OOM errors within my LXC containers. After updating to Deb13/PVE9.x I found some of my LXC containers at 99% CPU and 99% MEM usage.

Debian 13 has, by default, moved /tmp to a tmpfs.

It incorrectly pulls the amount of memory tmpfs has available as the host memory capacity, in my case 64GB; tmpfs defaults to size=50%. Meaning the LXC thinks it can use 50% of available memory for /tmp.
